paragraphs: Output format can be PNG (lossless, supports transparency), JPG (compact, no transparency) or WebP (compact, supports transparency). WebP is selected by default. Quality is a slider from 10 to 100, default 85, and applies to JPG and WebP only; PNG is lossless so the slider has no effect there. After conversion the tool lists the new dimensions and shows each file's size change, including when a result is larger than the original.

sections.heading: Choosing settings
paragraphs: Use JPG for photos that need to work everywhere and WebP when the destination supports it and you want smaller files. Use PNG for screenshots, logos and graphics with sharp edges or transparency. Converting a PNG photo to PNG again will not shrink it, and converting JPG to PNG will usually make the file larger without restoring lost detail. Repeated lossy conversions lower quality each time, so work from the original.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Only PNG, JPG and WebP files are accepted. Transparent areas turn white when saving as JPG. Drawing through a canvas means embedded metadata such as camera details, location and color profiles is not carried over, and animated images are not preserved, since only a single frame is drawn. Support for encoding WebP depends on your browser, and the tool shows an error if it cannot encode the format. Very large images use a lot of memory. Your file is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What JSON Formatter does
paragraphs: JSON Formatter takes JSON text and either lays it out with indentation, compresses it to a single line, or checks that it is valid. You can paste text or open a .json or plain text file. The output can be copied or downloaded as formatted.json.

sections.heading: Options
paragraphs: Three buttons run the tool: Format / Beautify, Minify JSON and Validate JSON. Indentation can be 2 spaces (default), 4 spaces or 1 space. Sort object keys alphabetically is an optional checkbox that orders keys at every level using locale-aware comparison. Validate reports success or the parser error message, and it also fills the output with the formatted text.

sections.heading: Practical notes
paragraphs: Sorting keys makes two versions of a file easier to compare, but it changes the order of keys, which matters only if something reads the order. Standard JSON does not allow comments, trailing commas, single-quoted strings or unquoted keys, and such input is reported as an error. The error message comes from your browser, so its wording and position information can vary. Minify removes only whitespace between values.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The tool uses the browser's built-in JSON parser. Numbers larger than a double-precision float can hold, such as very long IDs, may lose digits when parsed and written back, and duplicate keys in an object are collapsed to the last one. Very large files can make the page slow because the text is shown in the page. Nothing is checked against a schema. Your text is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Base64 Tool does
paragraphs: Base64 Tool has three modes: encode text to Base64, decode Base64 back to text, and calculate a hash of text or of a file. Everything is done in your browser with built-in functions, and results can be copied.

sections.heading: Modes and options
paragraphs: Encode converts text as UTF-8 so accented letters and symbols are handled correctly. Decode expects Base64 that represents UTF-8 text and reports an error if the result is not valid UTF-8, so it is not meant for binary data such as images. A URL-safe checkbox switches the alphabet to - and _ and removes padding when encoding; decoding accepts the same form. In Hash mode you choose text or a file and an algorithm: SHA-256 (default), SHA-384, SHA-512 or SHA-1. The result is shown as hexadecimal.

sections.heading: Practical notes
paragraphs: Base64 is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can reverse it, so do not use it to hide passwords. SHA hashes are one-way fingerprints, useful for checking that a downloaded file matches a published checksum. Compare the full string, and use SHA-256 or stronger where you can; SHA-1 is included for compatibility with older checksums. This tool does not offer MD5, and it cannot encode a file to Base64, only text.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: File hashing is limited to 100 MB to protect browser memory, and the whole file is read into memory before hashing. Hashing needs the browser's secure crypto feature, which is available on HTTPS pages and localhost. Spaces and line breaks in Base64 input are ignored when decoding. Your text and files are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Display Studio does
paragraphs: Display Studio turns PDFs, Word (.docx) files and images into a full-screen slideshow that you can run on a screen, TV or kiosk browser. Each PDF page, Word page or image becomes a slide that you can reorder, include or leave out, give a caption, and set its own duration.

sections.heading: Playback settings
paragraphs: The default slide duration is 10 seconds, adjustable from 1 to 86400 seconds, and each slide can have its own value. Options are loop (on by default), shuffle, picture fit (Contain, Cover or Stretch), transition (Cut, Fade or Slow zoom), background color, a clock and date overlay with 12 or 24 hour time and a choice of corner, a slide counter, and a request to keep the screen awake. Keyboard controls include arrow keys and Page Up and Page Down to move, and Space or P to pause.

sections.heading: Choosing settings
paragraphs: Contain shows the entire page and may leave bars; Cover fills the screen but can crop edges; Stretch can distort text. For notice-board PDFs, Contain with a dark background is the safest. Keep-awake uses the browser's screen wake lock where it is supported, and a message appears if it is not. Plan the first run in the same browser and screen you will use, including fullscreen, before relying on it.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Each file must be 100 MB or smaller. Slides are rendered once to images in memory, PDF pages at up to 1.6x scale (capped at 1600 px wide) as JPEG at 88 percent quality, so text in a PDF is no longer text on screen, and Word layout can differ from Word. Password-protected PDFs are refused with a message to unlock them first. Slides are held in memory while the page is open. Files are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What POS Invoice Studio does
paragraphs: POS Invoice Studio helps a small shop make a customer bill in the browser. You enter shop details and an inventory of items, add items to a bill with quantities, and the tool calculates the totals. You can print the bill or download it as a PNG image.

sections.heading: Shop and bill settings
paragraphs: Shop details include name, tagline, address, tax ID, phone, email and an invoice prefix (INV by default). The currency defaults to INR. You set a tax label (GST by default) and rate, an optional second tax with its own label and rate, an optional extra charge, and whether prices are tax exclusive or tax inclusive. Inventory items have a name, SKU, unit and price; units include pcs, box, pack, kg, g, lb, oz, L, mL, m and cm. Each bill has a number, date, customer name and contact, notes and line items.

sections.heading: How totals work
paragraphs: Each line is quantity times unit price, rounded to two decimals. With exclusive pricing, the taxes are added on top. With inclusive pricing, the tool works backwards from the line price to the taxable amount, and the total stays equal to the sum of line prices plus any charge. Taxes are calculated per line and rounded each time, so a total can differ by a cent from a system that rounds only at the end. Check the numbers against your local tax rules; the tool does not know any.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The tool is a bill maker. It does not file taxes, check GST numbers or keep sales reports. Printing uses your browser's print dialog, and the image export is a PNG capture of the bill. You can save a shop profile and inventory in your browser's own storage on this device, and download profile or bill files as JSON; clearing site data removes browser-saved profiles, so keep a downloaded copy. Data is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What the Income Tax Calculator does
paragraphs: It works out your tax for the year under both the old and the new regime from the same inputs and shows the two results side by side, with the lower one highlighted. You enter gross salary, other income, age group and, if you want to test the old regime properly, your deductions.

sections.heading: How the new regime is calculated
paragraphs: The tool applies the new regime slabs: nil up to ₹4 lakh, 5% to ₹8 lakh, 10% to ₹12 lakh, 15% to ₹16 lakh, 20% to ₹20 lakh, 25% to ₹24 lakh and 30% above. A standard deduction of ₹75,000 is taken from salary. If taxable income is ₹12 lakh or less, the rebate of up to ₹60,000 brings the tax to nil, and just above ₹12 lakh marginal relief stops the tax from exceeding the income above that limit. Surcharge and 4% cess are added on top.

sections.heading: How the old regime is calculated
paragraphs: The old regime uses the basic exemption limit for your age (₹2.5 lakh, ₹3 lakh for ages 60 to 79, ₹5 lakh from age 80) with 5% up to ₹5 lakh, 20% up to ₹10 lakh and 30% above. The standard deduction is ₹50,000, and the deductions you enter are capped at their usual limits. The rebate of up to ₹12,500 applies when taxable income is ₹5 lakh or less. Surcharge, with marginal relief, and cess follow.

sections.heading: The break-even point between the regimes
paragraphs: The comparison also shows how much in deductions and exemptions the old regime needs before it costs less than the new regime. That covers 80C, 80D, HRA, home loan interest and similar items. The standard deduction and employer NPS are already counted in both regimes, so they are not part of the figure.

Compare the break-even amount with what you can really claim. If you are above it, the old regime wins; if you are below it, the new regime does, and adding a small deduction rarely changes that. At some incomes the new regime wins at any level of deductions, and the calculator says so.

sections.heading: Limits of this estimate
paragraphs: Rules change every Budget, and this tool is a planning aid, not tax advice. It covers a resident individual with salary and slab-rate income only. Capital gains, business income, TDS already deducted, advance tax and special cases are not included. Check incometax.gov.in or consult a tax professional before you file.

sections.heading: What the Salary Calculator does
paragraphs: It turns an annual CTC figure into an estimated monthly in-hand salary. You enter CTC, the percentage of CTC that is basic salary, how PF is calculated, the tax regime and professional tax, and the tool shows what is left each month.

sections.heading: How the numbers are worked out
paragraphs: Employer PF (12% of basic, or of ₹15,000 a month if you cap it) is part of CTC but is not paid out, so it is removed first to get gross salary. Employee PF of the same amount, professional tax and income tax for FY 2026-27 are then deducted. The tax uses the same engine as the Income Tax Calculator.

sections.heading: Why your payslip may differ
paragraphs: Real salary structures vary. Variable pay and bonuses, gratuity, group insurance premiums, employer NPS and reimbursements are not modelled, and professional tax rules differ by state. Treat the result as a close estimate for comparing offers, not a promise of what will reach your account.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: The calculation runs in your browser as you type. Nothing you enter is uploaded to MyDailyUtils, although the page still loads advertising and other resources.

sections.heading: What the HRA Calculator does
paragraphs: It shows how much of the House Rent Allowance you receive is exempt from income tax. You enter monthly basic salary including dearness allowance, the monthly HRA you receive, the rent you pay and whether you live in a metro city.

sections.heading: The three-way rule
paragraphs: The exemption is the lowest of three figures: the HRA actually received; rent paid minus 10% of basic salary; and 50% of basic salary for metro cities or 40% for others. The tool lists all three so you can see which one limits you. The part of HRA above the exemption is taxable.

sections.heading: Things to remember
paragraphs: HRA exemption is only available under the old tax regime. You need to be paying rent, keep rent receipts, and give your landlord's PAN if yearly rent is above ₹1 lakh. Which cities count as metro is set by the tax rules, so confirm yours.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: The calculation runs in your browser and nothing you enter is uploaded to MyDailyUtils.

sections.heading: What the EMI Calculator does
paragraphs: It calculates the equated monthly instalment for a loan and shows how much interest you will pay overall. Enter the amount, yearly interest rate and tenure in years or months and the results update as you type.

sections.heading: How the schedule works
paragraphs: Each month, interest is charged on the outstanding balance and the rest of the EMI reduces the principal. Early instalments are mostly interest and later ones mostly principal. The table adds this up year by year so you can see how quickly the balance falls.

sections.heading: Using it to compare loans
paragraphs: Try a lower rate, a shorter tenure or a larger down payment and watch total interest change. A longer tenure lowers the EMI but raises the interest paid, so compare total payment, not just the monthly figure.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: Assumes a fixed rate, equal monthly instalments and no fees or part-prepayments. Your lender's schedule is the final word.

sections.heading: What the SIP Calculator does
paragraphs: It estimates how much a monthly systematic investment plan could grow to over time. You choose the monthly amount, an assumed yearly return and the number of years, and optionally a yearly step-up.

sections.heading: The assumptions
paragraphs: Instalments are made at the start of each month and the return compounds monthly at one-twelfth of the yearly rate. With a step-up, the monthly amount increases once a year by the percentage you set. The table shows invested amount and value at the end of each year.

sections.heading: Using the result sensibly
paragraphs: Real returns fluctuate, so try several rates rather than relying on one. Compare the gain with the amount invested and see how much a modest step-up or a few extra years changes the outcome. Tax on gains and fund costs are not included.

sections.heading: Value in today's money and goal mode
paragraphs: A big future number can mislead, because prices rise every year. Enter an expected yearly inflation rate and the calculator also shows what the final value is worth in today's money. The inflation figure is your own assumption, not a forecast, so try a few values.

If you already have a target, type it in the goal field. The calculator works backwards and shows the monthly SIP needed to reach it with the same return, years and yearly step-up. A step-up lowers the starting instalment you need, which is why it is worth trying.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: This is an illustration, not a forecast or investment advice. Past returns do not guarantee future results.

sections.heading: What the FD Calculator does
paragraphs: It works out the maturity value of a fixed deposit and the interest earned. Enter the deposit, the yearly rate, the period and how often interest is compounded.

sections.heading: How compounding changes the result
paragraphs: More frequent compounding means interest earns interest sooner, so the effective yearly yield is slightly higher than the quoted rate. The tool shows that effective yield next to the maturity amount.

sections.heading: Before you rely on it
paragraphs: Banks may round interest, use day-count rules, or pay interest out rather than reinvest it. Interest is taxable and TDS may apply. Check your bank's terms for the exact figure.

sections.heading: Tax and TDS on FD interest
paragraphs: FD interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate. Enter that rate and the calculator shows the tax, the maturity amount after tax and the yearly yield after tax, which is often what you should compare with other savings options.

Banks usually deduct TDS when the interest in a year is above a limit: ₹50,000 for most people and ₹1,00,000 for senior citizens, at the time of writing. The calculator warns you when your yearly interest is above the limit for the depositor type you choose. TDS is not an extra tax: it is credited against your final tax when you file your return. Limits and rules change, so confirm them with your bank.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: The calculation runs in your browser and nothing you enter is uploaded to MyDailyUtils.

sections.heading: What the PPF Calculator does
paragraphs: It projects how a PPF account could grow if you deposit the same amount each year. Choose the yearly deposit, the interest rate and the period, and the tool shows the balance, interest earned and maturity value.

sections.heading: The assumptions
paragraphs: The full yearly deposit is assumed to be made at the start of each financial year, before 5 April, so it earns interest for all twelve months. The rate is assumed constant, although the government reviews it every quarter. Interest is compounded yearly.

sections.heading: Why PPF is popular
paragraphs: PPF is a government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year lock-in, and contributions are eligible for deduction under Section 80C in the old tax regime. Check the current rules and rate with your bank or post office before investing.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: A real passbook may differ slightly because of monthly interest calculation and rate changes. This is a planning estimate, not advice.

sections.heading: What the GST Calculator does
paragraphs: It adds GST to a price, or takes GST out of a price that already includes it, and shows the price without GST, the GST amount, the total, and the CGST and SGST halves.

sections.heading: Adding and removing GST
paragraphs: To add GST, the tool multiplies the price by the rate. To remove it, it divides the inclusive amount by one plus the rate to find the base price, then treats the difference as GST. Quick buttons cover common rates such as 0%, 3%, 5%, 18% and 40%, and you can type any other rate.

sections.heading: CGST, SGST and IGST
paragraphs: In a sale within one state the GST amount is shared equally between CGST and SGST. In a sale to another state the whole amount is IGST. The calculator shows the half share so you can fill an invoice.

sections.heading: Finding a rate and splitting the tax
paragraphs: If you have a price without GST and the price with GST, choose Find the GST rate from two prices. The calculator shows the rate and the closest standard slab, which helps you check an invoice. If the result is not close to a standard rate, the prices may be rounded or the invoice may mix items.
Choose whether the sale is within one state or between states. Within a state the tax is split into equal CGST and SGST; between states the whole amount is IGST. The total is the same either way.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: The right rate depends on the item, and rates are revised by the GST Council, so confirm it before invoicing. Results are rounded to paise for display.

sections.heading: What Image Resizer does
paragraphs: Image Resizer reduces a picture to a maximum file size in KB and can also set an exact width and height. This tool re-encodes your picture as a JPG and searches for the highest quality that still fits under the size you choose, so the picture keeps as much detail as the limit allows.

sections.heading: Exact pixels, cropping and fit
paragraphs: If the form also asks for a specific width and height, tick the exact size option. You can crop the picture to fill the size from the centre, fit it inside the size with white borders, or stretch it. Cropping and fitting keep the proportions of the people and objects in the photo; stretching does not. When an exact size is set, only the quality is lowered to reach the limit.

sections.heading: If the limit cannot be reached
paragraphs: Very small limits on large or detailed pictures may be impossible to reach at that size. Without an exact size the tool scales the picture down in steps; with an exact size, try a larger limit or smaller pixel dimensions.
Every result shows its pixel size, its final file size and the quality used, so you can see what happened before you download.

sections.heading: Checking the result before you upload
paragraphs: Each result lists what it was checked against: the size against your limit, the exact width and height if you set them, and the JPG format. Tap the small picture to see it larger and check that the face or signature is clear. When you resize several images, Download all saves them one after another.
Portals often reject a photo for being too soft or cropped badly, even when the size is right, so the preview is worth a look.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: The output is always a JPG, and transparent areas become white. Some portals check the format or the exact pixel size as well as the file size, so read the instructions on the form. Camera and location data are not carried over. Your images are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Resize Image to 20 KB does
paragraphs: Many online forms, exam portals and application sites cap a photo or signature at about 20 KB. This tool re-encodes your picture as a JPG and searches for the highest quality that still fits under the size you choose, so the picture keeps as much detail as the limit allows.

sections.heading: If the limit cannot be reached
paragraphs: At 20 KB a detailed photo has little room. Scanned signatures and plain backgrounds compress far better than busy photos, so crop closely and avoid shadows.

sections.heading: What Resize Image to 50 KB does
paragraphs: A 50 KB limit is common for passport-style photos and ID uploads on government and job application portals. This tool re-encodes your picture as a JPG and searches for the highest quality that still fits under the size you choose, so the picture keeps as much detail as the limit allows.

sections.heading: If the limit cannot be reached
paragraphs: At 50 KB a passport-style photo at around 200 by 230 pixels usually fits comfortably; a full phone photo will be scaled down a lot, so crop first if you can.

sections.heading: What Resize Image to 100 KB does
paragraphs: Limits of 100 KB show up on application forms, profile pictures and document uploads. This tool re-encodes your picture as a JPG and searches for the highest quality that still fits under the size you choose, so the picture keeps as much detail as the limit allows.

sections.heading: If the limit cannot be reached
paragraphs: At 100 KB most phone photos fit after being scaled down moderately. If a result looks too soft, raise the limit slightly or reduce the pixel size yourself.

sections.heading: What Resize Image to 200 KB does
paragraphs: A 200 KB limit is a common ceiling for scanned documents, certificates and larger photos on upload forms. This tool re-encodes your picture as a JPG and searches for the highest quality that still fits under the size you choose, so the picture keeps as much detail as the limit allows.

sections.heading: If the limit cannot be reached
paragraphs: At 200 KB most photos and single-page scans fit with little visible loss. Text in scans stays readable better if you do not force a much smaller limit.

sections.heading: What Merge PDF does
paragraphs: Merge PDF joins two or more PDF files into one document. The pages of each file are copied in the order you choose, so the first page of your first file becomes page 1 of the result and the last page of your last file becomes the final page. The tool works with whole files, which makes it a good fit for combining a cover letter with an application, several scanned receipts into one expense report, or separate chapters into a single handout.

sections.heading: Getting the order right
paragraphs: After you add your files they appear in a list with up and down buttons. Use them to move a file earlier or later, and remove any file you added by mistake. The order of the list is the order of the finished PDF, so check it before you merge. If you need to rearrange individual pages inside the merged file, merge first and then use Organize PDF, or pull out the pages you want with Split PDF.

sections.heading: Tips for good results
paragraphs: Name your files so they sort sensibly before you add them, for example 01-cover.pdf and 02-form.pdf, so the list starts close to the right order. Very large PDFs, or many files at once, use a lot of memory on your device. If the page slows down or the merge fails, merge in smaller batches and then merge the results.

sections.heading: Using only some pages of a file
paragraphs: Each file shows its page count, and the merged file shows the total. In the Pages to use box under a file, type page numbers such as 1-3, 5 to take only those pages; leave it empty to take them all. The count under the box updates as you type, and a red note appears if nothing matches.
Use Sort A to Z when file names carry numbers, such as scan 2 and scan 10: they are ordered by number, not letter by letter. You can still move any file up or down afterwards.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Merge PDF has no fixed file-size limit of its own, but your browser and device memory set a practical one. Password-protected PDFs cannot be merged. If you know the password and are allowed to remove it, use Unlock PDF first. Your files are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Split PDF does
paragraphs: Split PDF takes the pages you choose from a PDF and saves them as a new PDF. You enter single page numbers, ranges or a mix, and the tool builds one new document containing exactly those pages. It is a quick way to pull a single form out of a long scan, to send only the relevant pages of a contract, or to cut a large document down before sharing it.

sections.heading: How to enter pages
paragraphs: After you choose a file the tool shows how many pages it has. Type page numbers separated by commas and use a hyphen for a range: 1, 4, 7 gives you three pages and 2-5 gives you pages two to five. You can combine both, such as 1-3, 7, 10-12. The pages come out in their original order whatever order you type them in, and a page you type twice is included once. Numbers outside the document are ignored, so check the page count shown before you extract.

sections.heading: Getting several separate files
paragraphs: The result is always a single PDF made from the pages you selected. To produce several separate files, run the tool once for each set of pages. If you want to remove pages rather than keep them, Delete PDF Pages is quicker, and Organize PDF lets you reorder, rotate or delete pages visually.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: A password-protected or damaged PDF may fail to load. Unlock PDF can remove a password if you know it and are allowed to. The downloaded file name includes the page selection and a timestamp, so you can keep several versions side by side. Your file is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Compress PDF does, and what it does not
paragraphs: Compress PDF makes a PDF smaller by removing information the document does not need in order to display, and by saving it with a more compact internal structure. It does not re-encode or shrink the pictures inside your file. Results therefore depend on what the PDF contains: documents with a lot of editing leftovers, thumbnails or metadata can get noticeably smaller, while a PDF made mostly of large scanned photos usually shrinks only a little.

sections.heading: The two optimization levels
paragraphs: Basic optimization is lossless. It clears document properties such as title, author, subject, keywords, creator and producer, and saves the file in a compact structure, so what you see on the pages does not change. Strong optimization does the same and also removes the document-level XMP metadata, editing data left behind by applications such as Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign, and the small preview thumbnails stored for each page. These items are not part of the visible page content. One side effect of clearing properties is that a PDF reader may no longer show a document title.

sections.heading: If the file is still too large
paragraphs: After compressing, the tool shows the original size, the new size and how much was saved. If the saving is small, the file size is probably dominated by images. In that case reduce the images before you build the PDF: shrink them with Image Compressor and combine them with Image to PDF, or scan at a lower resolution. If a form or portal asks for a file under a specific size, check the result before you upload it, or use Reduce to a size to fit a limit such as 200 KB.

sections.heading: Reduce to a size
paragraphs: Choose Reduce to a size when a portal or email limit gives a number, such as 100 KB, 200 KB or 1 MB. Type the size or tap a common limit. The tool first tries the lossless clean-up, which keeps text selectable. If the file is still too big, it turns each page into a picture and picks the sharpest combination of resolution and JPEG quality that fits.

The result says which method was used. When pages become pictures, text can no longer be selected, searched or copied, so keep the original for that. If even the smallest picture version is over your limit, the tool tells you how close it got and keeps the smallest result. A larger limit, or splitting the PDF into parts, is then the way forward.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Password-protected or damaged PDFs may fail to load. Keep your original file, since the compressed copy has its metadata removed. Your file is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What Image to PDF does
paragraphs: Image to PDF turns one or more pictures into a single PDF with each image on its own page. It accepts JPG, PNG and WebP images, which makes it useful for phone photos of documents, screenshots, receipts and scanned pages that arrived as images. The result is an ordinary PDF that you can email, print or upload to a form.

sections.heading: Choosing page size and margins
paragraphs: Choose A4 portrait, A4 landscape, US Letter or Fit to Image. A4 and US Letter give you standard page sizes for printing and for portals that expect them. Fit to Image makes each page the size of its picture and uses no margin. For the fixed sizes you can pick no margin, a small margin of 20 points or a standard margin of 40 points, where 72 points is one inch.

sections.heading: Order and file size
paragraphs: Images are added in the order you select them, and you can move any image up or down before you create the PDF. The tool does not apply extra lossy compression to your pictures, and WebP images are converted to PNG in your browser first, so the PDF will be about as large as the images you put in. To keep it small, reduce the pictures first with Image Compressor.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Only JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, so convert other formats first. Many high-resolution photos at once can be slow on a phone, so convert in smaller batches if the page struggles. Your images are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.

sections.heading: What PDF to Images does
paragraphs: PDF to Images turns every page of a PDF into a separate PNG image. Use it to share a single page as a picture, to place pages into a slide deck or chat, or to get image versions of a document for a tool that does not accept PDFs.

sections.heading: Quality and file size
paragraphs: Pages are rendered at twice their standard size, which gives sharp text and graphics for screens and most documents. PNG is lossless, so the images stay crisp, but a page with photos or heavy graphics can produce a large file. If you need smaller images, run the PNG files through Image Compressor and choose JPG or WebP.

sections.heading: Saving your pages
paragraphs: When the conversion finishes, each page appears with its own download button. Files are named after your PDF with the page number, for example report_page_3.png, so you can download only the pages you need.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: All pages are converted in one go, so a PDF with very many pages uses a lot of memory and may be slow on a phone. Password-protected or damaged PDFs may fail to convert. Your PDF is processed in your browser and is not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing. For some documents with non-Latin fonts, the PDF viewer library may download font mapping files from a public CDN, jsDelivr, but your document itself is not sent anywhere.

sections.heading: What Image Compressor does
paragraphs: Image Compressor reduces the file size of JPG, PNG and WebP images. You choose a quality, optionally limit the longest side of the picture, and optionally switch format. The tool shows how much smaller each result is, so you can decide before you save. It is handy for photos that are too large to email, to upload to a form, or to publish on a web page.

sections.heading: The settings that matter
paragraphs: Quality runs from 10 to 95 and controls lossy compression for JPG and WebP: lower values give smaller files with more visible artefacts. The maximum dimension option shrinks the picture so that its longest side is at most 2560, 1920, 1280 or 800 pixels, which often saves more than quality alone. For format you can keep the original where possible, or choose JPG (small for photos, no transparency), WebP (efficient, keeps transparency) or PNG (lossless, can be larger). With keep, PNG and WebP images stay as they are and JPG stays JPG.

sections.heading: Choosing settings
paragraphs: For photos, start at 75 percent quality and a longest side of 1920 pixels or less, then lower either one if the result is still too big. PNG is lossless, so the quality slider has no effect on PNG output. To shrink a PNG, reduce its dimensions or convert it to JPG or WebP. Screenshots and graphics with sharp edges usually look best as PNG or WebP. If a result comes out larger than the original, the tool tells you so, and you can try a lower quality or smaller dimensions.

sections.heading: Limits and privacy
paragraphs: Compression redraws the picture, so lossy formats lose some detail and information such as camera or location data is generally not carried over. Your original file is never changed. Very large images use a lot of memory, and formats other than JPG, PNG and WebP are not accepted. Your images are processed in your browser and are not uploaded to MyDailyUtils for processing.
